text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 antigen tests, often referred to as rapid tests, detect proteins (antigens) from the SARS-CoV-2 virus. They are quick and relatively inexpensive, providing results within 5-30 minutes, but are less sensitive than molecular tests like PCR. At-home antigen tests are authorized for serial testing, meaning multiple tests are needed over a period of time, especially if symptoms are present or if the initial test is negative.

list.title: What they detect:
list.snippet: COVID-19 rapid antigen tests look for specific proteins (antigens) on the surface of the SARS-CoV-2 virus.

list.title: How they work:
list.snippet: These tests are lateral flow assays, meaning the sample is applied to a test strip, and if the virus is present, it will bind to antibodies on the strip and produce a visible result, usually within 5-30 minutes.

list.title: Sensitivity:
list.snippet: While rapid and convenient, antigen tests are generally less sensitive than PCR tests, meaning they may not detect the virus as reliably, especially early in an infection or in people without symptoms.

list.title: Serial testing:
list.snippet: Because of their lower sensitivity, it is recommended to perform multiple antigen tests over several days, especially if you have symptoms or a negative result.
For example, if you have symptoms, it's recommended to test at least twice over three days.
If you don't have symptoms, it's recommended to test at least three times over five days.

list.title: When to use:
list.snippet: At-home antigen tests are useful for quickly assessing whether you might have COVID-19, especially if you have symptoms or have been exposed.
